name: Libertarian socialism
summary: Libertarian socialism is an anti-authoritarian, anti-capitalist current that seeks workers' self-management and direct democracy, rejecting both private ownership of the means of production and state ownership. It spans anarchist currents and libertarian Marxist ones such as council communism, and favours federated, decentralised organisation from below with direct action as its method.
scope: Libertarian socialism, as the defining scholarship uses the term: anti-authoritarian, anti-capitalist socialism that rejects both private ownership and state/party control, in Chomsky's account the heir of the Enlightenment's liberal ideals (s2, in Guérin's book, s5), and in Prichard et al. 'anti-parliamentary, democratic, anti-bureaucratic grass roots socialist organisation' located between anarchist and Marxist extremes (s6). The core is social anarchism (Proudhon, Bakunin, Kropotkin, Rocker) and libertarian Marxism / council communism (Pannekoek, Luxemburg, Korsch, Mattick), with later hybrids such as Socialisme ou Barbarie (Castoriadis); Goodway (s7) also applies the label to libertarian-socialist writers such as Morris, Wilde, Carpenter and Orwell who share many but not all anarchist traits. Individualist anarchism, market socialism and parliamentary democratic socialism are noted by these sources as outside it and are not followed.

keyWorks.title: The Soul of Man under Socialism
keyWorks.author: Oscar Wilde
keyWorks.quote:
‘The Soul of Man under Socialism’,
which appeared in February 1891, discusses first the problems of the present capitalist
society and its libertarian socialist reconstruction
